subject: Hospitality
title: The Pass: Command Central
description: A quick, practical guide to The Pass: Command Central.

hook.text: The pass is the counter between kitchen and dining room where finished plates are inspected before serving.

buildup.text: The head chef or expeditor stands at the pass, calling orders to stations, timing courses.

discovery.text: A single misfire at the pass—a wrong dish, a cold plate, a missing garnish—cascades into delays for the entire dining room.

twist.text: Heat lamps at the pass keep food warm but dry it out. A plate under lamps for 3+ minutes is a plate that shouldn't be served.

climax.text: The best expeditors are traffic controllers: calm under pressure, commanding without shouting.

punchline.text: Last checkpoint before the guest. Every plate lives or dies at the pass.

quiz.question: What is 'the pass' in a professional kitchen?
options: The counter where finished plates are inspected before being served to guests
